problem: Multilingual VLN agents (RxR: English, Hindi, Telugu) use pre-trained language/visual encoders that suffer domain shift and do not exploit the fact that instructions in different languages describe the same path. Agents also generalize poorly to unseen environments because visual encoders overfit low-level appearance, and prior environment-agnostic work only considers a single environment per path.
motivation: Paired multilingual instructions for one path share visual concepts and are complementary, so they can supervise a visually-grounded cross-lingual language representation. Instructions describing similar paths across different environments can serve as a bridge to learn appearance-invariant visual representations, reducing the seen/unseen gap.
key_idea: Pre-train the instruction encoder with contrastive learning on visually-aligned multilingual instruction pairs, and pre-train the visual encoder with contrastive learning on image pairs from semantically-similar paths in different environments (matched via instruction similarity and object-matching), before training the navigation agent.
insight: Both components contribute and are complementary: on RxR val-unseen with ResNet features, +text and +visual give small gains, while +both reaches SR 40.4 vs 35.1 baseline. Cross-lingual pairing matters: mono-lingual pairs hurt (SR 32.9 vs 36.0), and using only two of the three languages hurts even more. Object-matching constraints plus random sampling of 10 of the 27 classes improve nDTW (53.7 vs 52.4 without object constraints), and the visual representation reduces the seen-unseen nDTW gap from 1.6 to 1.0.
method: Cross-lingual language representation: fine-tune multilingual BERT with an InfoNCE contrastive loss on [CLS] embeddings of two randomly sampled instructions (possibly in different languages) for the same RxR path; the other 2(N-1) in-batch items serve as negatives.

Semantically-aligned path pair mining: for each instruction, find the most similar instruction (cosine on the learned representation) in the training set whose path has the same length; the two paths form a positive pair across environments.

Object-matching constraint: detect objects in the 36 views with Mask-RCNN (LVIS); keep 27 frequent classes, randomly sample 10 per iteration, and keep only view pairs at the same step that share an object from the sampled classes.

Environment-agnostic visual encoder: pre-trained ResNet-152 or CLIP ViT-B/32 features pass through two FC layers with ReLU, a residual connection and LayerNorm; the panorama is the mean of 36 views; contrastive loss maximizes the similarity of positive panorama pairs versus in-batch negatives.

Navigation learning: initialize the encoders from CLEAR and train the Tan et al. (EnvDrop-style) LSTM decoder with imitation learning (teacher actions from the GT path) plus A2C RL. Rewards include progress, nDTW and a ±3 stop reward, with loss L_RL + λL_IL.
Transfer: CLEAR representations are reused for R2R and CVDN, and further tuned on top of HAMT's released pre-trained weights.

setting.backbone: multilingual BERT-base + ResNet-152 / CLIP ViT-B/32 features + LSTM decoder (trained; representation pre-training then IL+RL)
setting.training_data: RxR training set (11,089 paths, ~126k instructions in en/hi/te); representation learning on the same data, plus Mask-RCNN (LVIS) object detections; no extra external data
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views: 12 headings x 3 elevations) plus instruction text
setting.privileged: none at test time (single-run, no pre-exploration); the GT path is used for training teacher actions

results: On the RxR test leaderboard (single run), CLEAR with CLIP features reaches nDTW 53.69, 2.59 above the mono-lingual CLIP agent of Shen et al. (51.10). On val-unseen, CLEAR-ResNet improves the baseline by 5.3 SR and 4.3 nDTW, and CLEAR-CLIP by 2.7 SR and 1.2 nDTW. Representations also transfer to R2R, CVDN and HAMT (+0.7 SR, +2.5 nDTW).
limitations: Only three languages (en/hi/te) are used, so generalization to other languages is unclear.
The multilingual agent is still weaker than mono-lingual agents, and the gains from CLEAR are modest with strong CLIP features.
The visual pair mining relies on instruction similarity plus a Mask-RCNN 27-class object detector, and paths are only loosely aligned.
